key_concepts: Force can change an object's shape by bending, cutting, crumpling, stretching, or pounding
Force can change an object's size by cutting, grinding, dropping, sharpening, or pounding.
Pushing or pulling is a force that can set an object into motion.
A still ball moves when a person touches it.
Greater mass requires greater force to move an object.
Moving a table requires greater force than moving a chair.
A stronger force makes a toy car move farther.
A soccer ball travels farther when kicked harder.
Pulling a rubber band harder stretches it longer.
Force affects the movement of an object.
